title: Sender continues issuing Chat/typing calls when recipient has opted out
description: The spec (draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md lines 438-439, 1416-1417) deliberately withholds opt-out status from the sender: Chat/typing always succeeds and the sender is not informed that receiveTypingIndicators is false on the recipient Chat record. Privacy rationale is sound. However the consequence is that a sending client in a direct chat with an opted-out recipient will continue calling Chat/typing at full rate (up to once per 3 seconds while typing) indefinitely. The server does a full membership check + preference lookup + silent discard on every call, with zero user-visible effect. No relief path exists: the server cannot hint 'don't bother' without revealing the preference, and the client has no other signal. In a long-lived session this is a steady stream of wasted client-to-server round-trips and per-call server work. The spec should consider whether server-side optimization (e.g. skipping rate-limit accounting for discarded events) is sufficient, or whether a privacy-preserving suppression hint is worth specifying. The implementer's guide should note this case so server authors can handle the discard path cheaply.
close_reason: Fixed in review fix wave or recorded as accepted design decision.
